overall: The AG found the Council violated the Open Meeting Law by failing to announce at its next meetings that certain executive session minutes would remain withheld and by not recording that in its minutes; the other allegations were not violations or were declined.

allegations.summary: Complaints alleged the Council failed to approve executive session minutes from December 8, 2015, December 11, 2018, and January 8, 2019 within the required timeframe.
allegations.key_passage: we are satisfied that each set of executive session minutes was approved in a timely manner

allegations.summary: Council reviewed December 8, 2015 executive session minutes at January meetings but did not announce or record at the next meetings that they would remain withheld.
allegations.key_passage: We find that the Council violated the Open Meeting Law by failing to announce at its meetings on January 22 and February 5 that the December 8, 2015, executive session minutes would continue to be withheld and by failing to include that determination in its minutes.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Council failed to release the December 8, 2015 executive session minutes once the purpose for secrecy had concluded.
allegations.key_passage: we decline to review this allegation because we have already decided the issue in a previous determination.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Council was required to review the January 8 executive session minutes at its January 22 meeting after a verbal request was made at a January 15 meeting.
allegations.key_passage: As such, we find that the Council did not violate the Open Meeting Law when it did not review the January 8 executive session minutes at its January 22 meeting.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Council failed to properly respond to an oral request for the January 8 executive session minutes made during a meeting.
allegations.key_passage: Here, the complainant did not make a formal, written request for the minutes nor indicate that he was making his request pursuant to the Open Meeting Law, but rather a verbal request in the midst of a meeting.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, including announcing at the next meeting after review whether executive session minutes remain withheld and recording that determination in the minutes.
remedy_passage: We order the Council’s immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, and we caution that similar future violations may be considered evidence of intent to violate the law.
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
